title: VP Student Affairs: "Give Me 20 Minutes" on Riverside

fields.orgName: Marlowe State University — Emergency Operations Center
fields.systemName: Recorded Line - EOC Room 108, Campus Services Building, Conference Bridge

caller.name: Vice President for Student Affairs
caller.label: Office of the Vice President for Student Affairs (cell)

callee.name: Director of Emergency Management, Incident Commander
callee.label: EOC Room 108 — IC position; Dean of Students joined 07:37

transcript.speaker: VP Student Affairs
transcript.text: Good morning. It's Student Affairs. I've seen the 07:20 forecast email. Do you have a minute? I know you don't really, so I'll be quick.

transcript.speaker: VP Student Affairs
transcript.text: I know the plan says a forecast crest of 10.5 or higher within three hours is enough to order Riverside out. And I know 10.8 near 10:30 is on paper. But that forecast went up 2.3 feet in one jump. Two point three feet, in one issuance.

transcript.speaker: VP Student Affairs
transcript.text: If I wake 680 students and march them through the rain at dawn, and the 9 AM issuance drops the crest a foot, I'll be explaining that to the President by lunch.

transcript.speaker: VP Student Affairs
transcript.text: So can you give me 20 minutes? Call NWS Charleston and the county EMA, ask them how confident they are in that number, and then decide. Twenty minutes. That's all I'm asking.

transcript.speaker: Riverside Hall Director
transcript.text: Dean? It's Riverside. The desk said you're in room 108, so they put me through on this line. Sorry to cut in.

transcript.speaker: Riverside Hall Director
transcript.text: I have 11 floors and one working stair tower lobby. My RAs say a full sweep with the elevators running is about 90 minutes. Without elevators, floors 9 to 11 take a lot longer.

transcript.speaker: Riverside Hall Director
transcript.text: And I have two residents on oxygen concentrators and a deaf resident on our access list. The RAs are already standing in the lobby with their floor sheets.

transcript.speaker: Riverside Hall Director
transcript.text: So if you're going to tell me to go, tell me now. Please.

voiceStyles.VP Student Affairs: Senior administrator, 50s, calm and courteous but firm, slightly hurried, speaking from a quiet office
voiceStyles.Riverside Hall Director: Residence hall director, 30s, tense and businesslike, lobby noise and students' voices behind them

instructorNote: This is the decision point. Under EOP 5, step 3, the 0720 AM forecast already meets the trigger for ordering Riverside out. The real choice is whether to order now or wait about 20 minutes to check how confident NWS and the county are, while the sweep's clearance time plus the margin means the order has to go out by about 08:00. SimCell reads the VP's lines, pauses at the prompt line for the IC's answer, then reads the Riverside lines and pauses for the Dean of Students. Watch whether the IC logs the time, the forecast issuance and the reason, and whether the Dean of Students tells the Riverside director to clear the access list (oxygen users and the deaf resident) first.
